fields.title: Kidney cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Kidney cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Kidney cancer is a serious condition that requires prompt diagnosis and effective treatment. Israel is one of the world leaders in oncology, offering advanced treatments for kidney cancer that help maximise the chances of a full recovery and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of kidney cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    is a quick, non-invasive method that can reveal tumours in the kidneys.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    help establish the size, shape and extent of the tumour and whether there are metastases.
  3. Kidney biopsy
    a procedure in which a sample of tissue is taken from the tumour for histological analysis. This allows the type of cancer to be established precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Laboratory tests of blood and urine
    can reveal changes indicating the presence of kidney cancer.
  5. PET-CT
    may be used for a more precise assessment of how far the kidney cancer has spread and for planning treatment.

Treatments for kidney cancer

  1. Surgery:
    • Radical nephrectomy — removal of the kidney together with the tumour.
    • Partial nephrectomy — removal of the tumour alone, preserving as much healthy kidney tissue as possible.
    • Robot-assisted surgery using the da Vinci system — an advanced technology delivering great surgical precision, less pain after the operation and a shorter recovery period.
  2. Ablation and cryoablation
    minimally invasive methods used to destroy the tumour by freezing or heating the tissue.
  3. Targeted therapy
    is aimed at blocking particular molecular pathways that help cancer cells grow and spread.
  4. Immunotherapy
    stimulates the body's immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  5. Radiotherapy
    may be used to ease symptoms and reduce pain, particularly in metastatic kidney cancer.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of kidney cancer

  • An individual approach to the treatment of every patient, taking account of every feature of their illness.
  • Highly qualified specialists and the use of advanced medical equipment ensure accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Multidisciplinary teams of doctors develop comprehensive treatment plans, combining various therapies to achieve the best results.
  • Value for money makes Israel an attractive destination for cancer patients from all over the world.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatments for kidney cancer, focusing on meeting patients' needs as fully as possible and on preserving and improving their quality of life.

fields.title: Pancreatic cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Pancreatic cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Pancreatic cancer is one of the most difficult cancers to treat, partly because it is often diagnosed late and progresses quickly. Israeli clinics offer advanced approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of this disease, using the latest advances in medical science to extend patients' lives and improve their quality of life.

Diagnosis of pancreatic cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    provide detailed images of the pancreas, helping identify a tumour and assess how far it has spread.
  2. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)
    produces high-quality images of the pancreas and surrounding tissues and also allows a biopsy to be taken.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count, biochemistry and blood tests for the tumour markers CA 19-9 and CEA, which may indicate the presence of pancreatic cancer.
  4. Biopsy
    followed by histological analysis of the tissue sample is the definitive method of diagnosing pancreatic cancer
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  5. PET-CT
    is used to assess metastases and the effectiveness of treatment.

Treatments for pancreatic cancer

  1. Surgery,
    including the Whipple procedure, is the main treatment for resectable forms of pancreatic cancer.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used both before the operation, to shrink the tumour, and afterwards, to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Radiotherapy
    may be used in combination with chemotherapy for local control of the disease.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new possibilities in the treatment of pancreatic cancer, particularly for patients with certain genetic mutations.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of pancreatic cancer

  • A multidisciplinary approach ensures a comprehensive assessment of the patient's condition and the development of an individualised treatment plan.
  • Highly qualified specialists and modern equipment guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to take every aspect of the illness and the patient's preferences into account when choosing treatments.
  • Research programmes and clinical trials give access to the newest treatments, which may not be available in other countries.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatments for pancreatic cancer, from surgery through to the newest protocols in chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy, aiming to extend each patient's life as far as possible and improve its quality.

fields.title: Oral cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Oral cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Oral cancer covers tumours that develop in the lips, tongue, floor of the mouth, gums, cheeks or palate. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, using modern technology and innovative methods to deliver the best possible results.

Diagnosis of oral cancer:

  1. Examination and biopsy:
    The doctor carries out a visual examination of the mouth and takes a biopsy of any suspicious areas for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  2. Endoscopy of the mouth and throat:
    Allows doctors to see the internal structures of the mouth and throat in order to assess the spread of the cancer.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT):
    Used to establish how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether there are metastases.
  4. PET-CT:
    Helps assess the activity of the tumour and detect distant metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests can reveal general indicators of health and of the functioning of organs that may be affected by the cancer.

Treatments for oral cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Excision of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue to prevent recurrence.
    • Neck dissection: Removal of the lymph nodes of the neck where the cancer has spread.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • External beam radiotherapy: Used to destroy any cancer cells remaining after surgery, or as the main treatment.
    • Brachytherapy: Internal irradiation, in which radioactive sources are placed directly in the tissue affected by the cancer.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in combination with radiotherapy or as an addition to surgery, to control metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Medicines directed at specific biological pathways involved in the growth and development of cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: The use of medicines to stimulate the body's immune system to attack the cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiotherapists and other specialists work together to create an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest technology in diagnosing and treating cancer.
  • An individual approach to every patient: Treatment plans are developed with each patient's personal needs and clinical data in mind.

Treatment of oral cancer in Israel aims to minimise the risk of recurrence, improve functional outcomes and give every patient the best possible quality of life.

fields.title: Penile cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Penile cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Penile cancer is a rare condition that requires a comprehensive approach to treatment, including surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Israeli clinics offer innovative treatments aimed at preserving function and minimising the psychological consequences for the patient.

Diagnosis of penile cancer:

  1. Visual examination and palpation:
    The first method for identifying visible abnormalities on the skin of the penis.
  2. Biopsy:
    Taking a tissue sample for examination under the microscope to confirm the presence of cancer cells.
  3. Ultrasound of the penis:
    Used to assess how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether it has spread to nearby structures.
  4. MRI and CT:
    Needed to establish the stage of the cancer and plan treatment.
  5. PET-CT:
    Carried out to identify metastases in the lymph nodes and other organs.

Treatments for penile cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Partial or total penectomy: Removal of part or all of the penis, depending on the stage and extent of the cancer.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Removal of the lymph nodes in the groin where metastases are suspected.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where surgery is not possible, or to reduce the risk of recurrence after an operation.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in advanced cancer or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of the newest medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
    • Activation of the immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Urologists, oncologists and radiotherapists coordinate their efforts to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • The use of modern technology: Access to advanced medical equipment and treatments.
  • Preserving quality of life: Particular attention is given to functional and cosmetic results after treatment, and to supporting patients at every stage of therapy.

Treatment of penile cancer in Israel aims for the greatest possible effectiveness while preserving function and minimising psychological distress for patients.
